references.text: Prohibition against practicing divination and interpreting omens, which is part of the same legislation against occult practices
Prohibition against seeking out mediums and spiritists, related to the prohibition against sorcery
The Lord will turn against those who seek out mediums and spiritists
Death penalty for anyone who practices mediumship or divination, parallel to the punishment for witches
Comprehensive list of forbidden occult practices, including sorcery, which is detestable to the Lord
Saul had driven out the mediums from the land, yet he still sought out the woman at En-Dor
Jezebel is mentioned for her sorcery, showing that witchcraft was still practiced and condemned
King Manasseh practiced sorcery and mediumship, which was evil in the Lord's sight
Sorcery is listed among the works of the flesh that exclude one from God's kingdom
Those who practice sorcery will receive their portion in the lake of fire, the final judgment on such practices
Sorcerers are among those kept outside the holy city
Micah confirms and expands Exodus' principles that witchcraft must be completely eradicated from God's people.
Isaiah uses the 'witch' motif from the law as a metaphor for national spiritual decay.
